cautions.text: This is a single-cell Li-Ion/Li-Polymer charger. VBAT is the connection to the cell's positive terminal. STAT is a status output; leaving PROG open or floating disables charging.
cautions.quote: If the PROG pin is open or floating, the MCP73831/2 are disabled

cautions.text: STAT is a status output for an LED or a host, and VBAT connects to the cell's positive terminal.
cautions.quote: STAT is an output for connection to an LED for charge

cautions.text: VBAT is the connection to the cell's positive terminal, not a second input supply.
cautions.quote: Connect to positive terminal of battery.

cautions.text: Do these checks with no cell connected.

cautions.text: A MOSFET has a body diode, so a diode-mode check from source to drain conducts one way; that is not a fault.
The body diode is a real path: a source-to-drain reading in one direction is that diode, not a damaged FET.
On the 3-lead SOT-23 top view the drain is the single lead at the top, the gate is on the left and the source is on the right.
The usual SOT-23 pin table numbers pin 1 gate, pin 2 source and pin 3 drain.

This is a Darlington: two transistors in one package with built-in base-emitter shunt resistors. A plain transistor test misleads — the base-emitter path reads more than one diode drop and has a resistor in parallel.
cautions.quote: Monolithic Construction with Built−In Base−Emitter Shunt Resistors

cautions.text: The base-emitter on-voltage is specified for the Darlington pair, not a single junction.
A diode-mode check from source to drain that conducts one way is the body diode, not a short.
